prompt: Each Scrum artifact has a commitment. Order the artifacts as work flows through them, from first to last.

task.prompt: Drag the items into the right order, first at the top.
task.explanation: Items are pulled from the Product Backlog into the Sprint Backlog, and become part of the Increment once they meet the Definition of Done.

prompt: Here is a team's Definition of Done for a client mobile app. Mark the lines that do not belong in a Definition of Done.

task.prompt: Mark every segment that is a problem. Leave the sound ones unmarked.

segments.text: Code reviewed and merged to the main branch.
Done if the developer is confident it works.
segments.issue: Not verifiable; the DoD must be objective checks anyone can confirm.

segments.text: Skip testing when the Sprint is running late.
segments.issue: The DoD is a quality bar; relaxing it under pressure creates hidden undone work.

prompt: On the last day of the Sprint, two stories are 'code complete' but have not been tested on staging, which your Definition of Done requires.

task.prompt: On the last day of the Sprint, two stories are 'code complete' but have not been tested on staging, which your Definition of Done requires.

steps.question: Can they be shown as Done at the Sprint Review?
options: No, they are not part of the Increment until they meet the Definition of Done
Yes, code complete is close enough
Yes, if the client agrees
Only one of them
steps.explanation: Work that does not meet the DoD cannot be released or presented as Done.

steps.question: What happens to them?
options: They return to the Product Backlog for the Product Owner to reorder
They count as Done and are tested later
They are deleted
The Sprint is extended by two days
steps.explanation: Undone items go back to the Product Backlog; the Sprint length does not change.

prompt: At the end of a Sprint, the Sprint Backlog had these items. Only items that meet the Definition of Done count. How many points are Done and what share of the planned points is that?

task.prompt: Calculate each value from the data.
task.explanation: Done items: 5 + 3 + 8 = 16 points. Planned: 5 + 3 + 8 + 5 + 2 + 3 = 26. Share = 16 / 26 = 61.5%. 'Code complete' and 'In QA' items do not count.

prompt: Review this Sprint Backlog summary posted to the client. Mark the lines that misuse the Scrum artifacts.

task.prompt: Mark every segment that is a problem. Leave the sound ones unmarked.

segments.text: Sprint Goal: customers can pay for an order with a saved card.
Selected items: save card, pay with saved card, payment receipts.
Plan: tasks broken down by the Developers on the board.
The Product Owner will add three new features to this Sprint Backlog on Wednesday.
segments.issue: The Sprint Backlog belongs to the Developers; new items can be negotiated but the PO cannot push scope in mid-Sprint without them.

segments.text: No Product Goal has been defined yet; we will decide after launch.
segments.issue: The Product Backlog's commitment is the Product Goal; without it the backlog has no direction.

segments.text: Increment will be deployed to staging when it meets the Definition of Done.

prompt: Order these Product Backlog items as a Product Owner should, for an app whose Product Goal is 'first paying customers by launch'.

task.prompt: Drag the items into the right order, first at the top.
task.explanation: Ordering follows value toward the Product Goal: no revenue without checkout, confirmations support paying customers, promotions help adoption, dark mode is nice to have.

prompt: What is the commitment for the Sprint Backlog?

options: The Sprint Goal
The Product Goal
The Definition of Done
The release date
mcq.explanation: Scrum Guide 2020: Product Backlog → Product Goal, Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal, Increment → Definition of Done.

options: A concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal that meets the Definition of Done
Any code written during the Sprint
The list of items for the next Sprint
A sprint report sent to the client
mcq.explanation: An Increment is usable, Done work; it adds to all prior Increments.

prompt: Your agency serves several client apps with different teams. Where should the Definition of Done come from?

options: The organisation's standard if one exists; otherwise the Scrum Team creates one appropriate for the product
Each developer decides their own
The client's legal department
It is optional in Scrum
mcq.explanation: If the organisation has a DoD standard, teams follow it as a minimum; otherwise the Scrum Team creates one.
